[page[title]]

A dependency must inherit an external type or implement an external interface that the application cannot control.

What the Standard says

“Dependency” — A dependency represents an external capability the application relies upon but cannot control. Local code should only model such a dependency when it must inherit or implement that external contract, and brokers are the components that consume it. read it here.

Why it matters

A Dependency element is justified only when the application must inherit or implement an external type it cannot control. Requiring that evidence prevents complex internal logic from being hidden in a class merely labelled Dependency to escape the Standard's service rules.

Bad code example

internal class RoslynDependency
{
    // Complex local Roslyn processing does not make this a dependency.
}

Good code example

internal class SchoolDbContext(
    DbContextOptions<SchoolDbContext> options)
    : DbContext(options)
{
}
